issues.description: Error handling complects message-processing with connection-loss recovery
issues.detail: The fix removes the outer try/except so socket-close exceptions now propagate up through _receive_messages. That intertwines two distinct concerns: per-message parse errors (handled inline) and connection-lifecycle events (now implicit). The caller's reconnect loop becomes the de facto handler for disconnect, but nothing names that contract. Separate them: let parse errors stay inline, and let disconnect be an explicit return/signal, not an unnamed exception bubble.

issues.description: Error message types are data, not code; the giant elif tuple is place-oriented
issues.detail: Fourteen string literals hardcoded into an elif branch is exactly the incidental complexity the problem doesn't require. The set of known error types is a value — a set or dict mapping type to display prefix. Lift it to module-level data and the dispatch becomes a one-line membership check. Then adding a new error type is data, not code.

issues.description: Duplicate transcriber_error entry reveals the listing-as-code smell
issues.detail: transcriber_error appears twice in the tuple. The compiler doesn't care, but the duplication is evidence that humans are maintaining what should be a set. If this were data (a set literal) the duplicate would either be harmless deduplication or caught by a one-line assertion. EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: copy-paste felt easy; the resulting list is not simple.

issues.description: Lost per-type log granularity by collapsing auth/quota into generic Error
issues.detail: Previously auth_error and quota_exceeded logged with distinct prefixes (Auth error, Quota exceeded). Now everything is Error: with the type only appearing if data.get('error') is missing. Operators reading logs lose the categorical signal. If the error-types-as-data refactor lands, the mapping can carry a display label per type at zero added complexity.

issues.description: The two changes in one PR are separable concerns
issues.detail: The infinite-loop fix and the error-type expansion are independent values. They share a file but not a problem. Landing them together makes bisect harder and complects the changelog. Not blocking, but worth noting that 'one PR, one concept' would have made both easier to reason about.

review.summary: The infinite-loop fix is correct in effect but achieves it by removing the swallowing try/except, which silently changes the contract between _receive_messages and its caller's reconnect loop — a complecting of message-processing and connection-lifecycle that should be named explicitly. The error-handling expansion replaces three specific branches with a fourteen-string elif tuple (one duplicated), which is the textbook case of code-where-data-belongs: lift the known error types to a module-level set or mapping and dispatch becomes trivial. The patch is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: each change is small and familiar, but neither separates the concerns it touches. The shape I'd prefer is explicit disconnect signaling and error types as data, in two separate PRs.
